claims.text: Early pregnancy: timeline Gestational sac: usually seen at about 4 to 5 weeks (serum beta-hCG about 1500 mIU/mL); yolk sac usually by 5 weeks
claims.quote: Presence of a gestational sac in the uterus, typically visible on ultrasound at about 4 to 5 weeks and typically corresponding to a serum beta-hCG level of about 1500 mIU/mL (a yolk sac can usually be seen in the gestational sac by 5 weeks)

claims.text: Fetal heart motion: as early as 5 to 6 weeks
claims.quote: Fetal heart motion visualized on ultrasound as early as 5 to 6 weeks

claims.text: Intrauterine or ectopic? Intrauterine pregnancy (diagnostic): a gestational sac with a yolk sac or an embryo (with or without heartbeat) inside the uterine cavity
claims.quote: Ultrasonographic findings diagnostic of an intrauterine pregnancy are a gestational sac with a yolk sac or an embryo (with or without a heartbeat) within the uterine cavity.

claims.text: Suggests ectopic: no intrauterine pregnancy, plus a complex (mixed solid and cystic) mass, especially in the adnexa, and echogenic free fluid in the cul-de-sac
claims.quote: In addition to absence of an intrauterine pregnancy, ultrasonographic findings suggesting ectopic pregnancy include a complex (mixed solid and cystic) pelvic mass, particularly in the adnexa, and echogenic free fluid in the cul-de-sac.

claims.text: Discriminatory zone: above this beta-hCG level a gestational sac with yolk sac should be seen; the recommended threshold is now 3500 mIU/mL
claims.quote: If serum beta-hCG is above a certain level (called the discriminatory zone), ultrasonography should be able to detect a gestational sac with a yolk sac; the presence of a yolk sac confirms an intrauterine pregnancy. The appropriate hCG threshold for the discriminatory zone for women with suspected ectopic pregnancy has been reevaluated. To minimize overdiagnosis of ectopic pregnancy and preserve desired intrauterine pregnancies, the recommended threshold has been increased to 3500 mIU/mL)

claims.text: Below the zone with a normal ultrasound, it may be an early intrauterine pregnancy or an ectopic
claims.quote: If the beta-hCG level is below the discriminatory zone and ultrasonography is unremarkable, patients may have an early intrauterine pregnancy or an ectopic pregnancy.

claims.text: Later pregnancy Ultrasound follows fetal growth and development and finds placental problems such as placenta previa
claims.quote: Pregnancy: For example, to evaluate the growth and development of the fetus and to detect abnormalities of the placenta (eg, placenta previa
